Finding rationale:
The Base Agreement runs for an initial three-year term (p0104) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause - material breach, insolvency, competitor acquisition, or continuing force majeure (p0107 to p0118). No convenience exit exists for IBM anywhere: Section 4.0's six-month notice is natural-term non-renewal (RENEWAL, not T4C) and SOW Section 6.1 reaches individual Purchase Orders only, subject to cost reimbursement. Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is a missing-behaviour deviation, so we insert operative language: 'IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL', with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. The narrow 'Notwithstanding Section 5.1' opener prevents MSL from reading the retained for-cause preamble as exclusive, without deleting or rewriting Section 5.1. Direction is checked: MSL has no mid-term convenience right because Section 5.1 confines termination by either Party to cause, so preferred element 4 is already met and no new restriction on MSL is drafted. Placement inside Section 5.0 preserves Section 4.0's cross-reference, and Sections 5.2, 5.3 and SOW 6.1 survive unchanged. 60 to 90 days' notice remains the fallback concession.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: The only exit-assistance obligation is Section 5.2 a) ii) (\"assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products ... to IBM or to another party that IBM designates\"), which is (i) gated by the chapeau in p0121 to expiration or termination for default rather than any termination, and (ii) has no committed duration, so it fails the fallback requirement of at least 90 days of transition assistance. The return obligation in Section 5.2 a) iii) is limited to IBM Product documentation and confidential media, runs on a redacted \"[*] Days\" period, and is not a data export within a fixed 30 days. Section 12.0/Supplement 1 Transition Services are inbound only (they expired December 31, 1998) and Attachment 6/Section 12.1 cover software master media and Loaned Items, not our data. We therefore inserted the shortest fallback clause: 90 Days of assistance after any expiry or termination plus a 30-Day export of all IBM data. We did not pursue the preferred six-month/then-current-rates/certified-deletion package.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.",
  "Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.",
  "Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.",
  "Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty."
]

{"sectionRef":"§ ATTACHMENT 1","cursor":0,"totalParagraphs":10,"nextCursor":null,"paragraphs":[{"id":"p0868","text":"ATTACHMENT 1"},{"id":"p0869","text":"IBM/MSL Outsourcing Base Agreement Statement of Work"},{"id":"p0870","text":"11.2 Each month IBM will provide MSL, one rolling [*] month forecast by machine type, model, and by geography. This forecast will be MSL's authorization to order/purchase Parts only for the fulfillment of orders, in accordance to the IBM published lead-times for such materials. Products shall be produced and delivered according to actual intake of IBM Customer Orders. MSL will participate in the process of requirements planning by giving the best Product supply projection and participating in cross functional meetings when required."},{"id":"p0871","text":"The following will apply:"},{"id":"p0872","text":"a) The forecast will contain anticipated Delivery Dates for specified quantities of machine types, models and geographies and lead-time profile updates, as required, for specific Parts."},{"id":"p0873","text":"b) MSL will notify IBM within [*] Days of receipt of a forecast if MSL is unable to meet the quantities and Delivery Dates. If MSL fails to notify IBM within the [*] Days, MSL will be deemed to have accepted the quantities and Delivery Dates and will be bound by them; provided, however, that MSL's actual or deemed acceptance of any forecast shall be subject to the availability of IBM Parts and IBM Designated Parts as needed, and MSL shall not be subject to any penalties (and IBM shall not be able to reject any proposed rescheduling of Delivery Dates) under this Agreement for failure to meet Delivery Dates due to the unavailability of such Parts at the times necessary to meet Delivery Dates, provided further however that such unavailability of IBM Parts or IBM Designated Parts is not due to MSL's failure to properly order such Parts or otherwise properly manage its relationship with the provider of such Parts."},{"id":"p0874","text":"c) If MSL notifies IBM that it cannot meet the quantities and Delivery Dates in IBM's forecast, MSL's notification will include the quantities MSL can deliver within the forecast's Delivery Dates and proposed schedule of Delivery Dates for delivering the quantities MSL cannot deliver within the forecast. IBM shall notify MSL in writing, within [*] Days of receipt of MSL's notification, of its decision either, in its sole discretion to:"},{"id":"p0875","text":"i) agree to the quantities and Delivery Dates in MSL's notification, which will then become binding upon both parties; or"},{"id":"p0876","text":"ii) agree to the quantities that will meet the forecast's Delivery Dates, which will then become binding on both parties, and either begin good faith negotiations with MSL to resolve any shortfall or reject MSL's proposed schedule for the remaining quantities; or provided, however that IBM may not reject MSL's proposed schedules if the reason for MSL's inability to meet the Delivery Dates is directly attributable to a breach of this Agreement by IBM. MSL may, with IBM's prior written approval and at MSL's expense, employ another manufacturer for the quantities that MSL cannot deliver within the forecast for the affected products. Notwithstanding any other term of this Agreement, if IBM rejects all or any part of MSL's proposal, IBM shall also be free to seek"},{"id":"p0877","text":"IBM Confidential Page 21 of 39 sow0501.lwp"}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ 11.3 Feature Forecast","cursor":0,"totalParagraphs":3,"nextCursor":null,"paragraphs":[{"id":"p0883","text":"11.3 Feature Forecast"},{"id":"p0884","text":"a) MSL agrees to perform all feature forecasting as part of their responsibilities. MSL agrees to forecast features in full support of the requirements forecast that IBM passes at a machine type level per Section 11.1 above."},{"id":"p0885","text":"b) MSL will notify IBM within [*] Days of receipt of the monthly requirements forecast, at the machine type level, if MSL is unable to support the features necessary to meet the Delivery Dates of the machine types per Section 11.1 above of this Agreement."}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ 13.2 Supply Flexibility","cursor":0,"totalParagraphs":6,"nextCursor":null,"paragraphs":[{"id":"p0922","text":"13.2 Supply Flexibility"},{"id":"p0923","text":"a) MSL will ensure flexibility for volumes, as specified in the Supply Flexibility Appendix 4."},{"id":"p0924","text":"b) Quarterly, MSL will update IBM on progress in improving Supplier Flexibility."},{"id":"p0925","text":"c) IBM will use commercially reasonable efforts to transfer LSS and SSS arrangements with IBM suppliers to MSL."},{"id":"p0926","text":"d) [*] months before EOL, MSL and IBM will agree on a transition plan to regulate the flexibility."},{"id":"p0927","text":"e) Cost of the Supply Flexibility as defined in Appendix 4 is included in Product pricing per Section 7.0. IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility."}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ 13.3 End of Life (\"EOL\") Inventory","cursor":0,"totalParagraphs":3,"nextCursor":null,"paragraphs":[{"id":"p0928","text":"13.3 End of Life (\"EOL\") Inventory"},{"id":"p0929","text":"a) IBM agrees to share an annual plan with quarterly updates on product EOL activity. Included will be the following scheduled events: product withdrawal, end of manufacture, and transfer to IBM, if applicable."},{"id":"p0930","text":"b) MSL agrees to provide inventory planning support and squared set analysis on these inventories participating in EOL activities prior to any transfer to IBM. {"sectionRef":"§ 13.4 Sale of Inventory","cursor":0,"totalParagraphs":2,"nextCursor":null,"paragraphs":[{"id":"p0931","text":"13.4 Sale of Inventory"},{"id":"p0932","text":"MSL agrees not to sell excess or surplus inventory purchased by MSL in support of this Agreement without the prior written approval of IBM which shall not be unreasonably withheld."}]}

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**TRANSITION — deviation (fallback cure inserted).**

- **What exists:** Section 5.2 a) ii) requires MSL to "assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products … to IBM or to another party that IBM designates," but the chapeau (p0121) limits Section 5.2 a) to "expiration or termination **for default**," and no duration is committed. Section 5.2 a) iii) returns only IBM Product documentation and confidential media on a redacted "[*] Days" clock — not a data export within a fixed 30 days.
- **What doesn't:** Section 12.0 / Supplement 1 "Transition Services" are inbound-only and expired 31 Dec 1998; Attachment 6 §3 (MS Software Image media) and §12.1 (Loaned Items) are asset-return, not exit assistance or data return.
- **Cure:** one new Section 5.2 d) carrying exactly the three fallback elements — any-reason expiry/termination trigger, ≥90 Days of assistance (by cross-reference to the existing 5.2 a) ii) obligation, so nothing is duplicated), and a 30-Day export of all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for IBM. Preferred extras (six months, then-current rates, machine-readable format, certified deletion) were deliberately not volunteered.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"fallback","mappings":[{"element":"Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]}]}

Finding rationale:
The only exit-assistance obligation is Section 5.2 a) ii) (\"assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products ... to IBM or to another party that IBM designates\"), which is (i) gated by the chapeau in p0121 to expiration or termination for default rather than any termination, and (ii) has no committed duration, so it fails the fallback requirement of at least 90 days of transition assistance. The return obligation in Section 5.2 a) iii) is limited to IBM Product documentation and confidential media, runs on a redacted \"[*] Days\" period, and is not a data export within a fixed 30 days. Section 12.0/Supplement 1 Transition Services are inbound only (they expired December 31, 1998) and Attachment 6/Section 12.1 cover software master media and Loaned Items, not our data. We therefore inserted the shortest fallback clause: 90 Days of assistance after any expiry or termination plus a 30-Day export of all IBM data. We did not pursue the preferred six-month/then-current-rates/certified-deletion package.

p0129: ii) assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products as described in Attachment 1: Statement Of Work, to IBM or to another party that IBM designates.

This shall include Parts purchased and to be delivered to MSL to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, subject to the Supply Flexibility set forth in Appendix 4 to the Statement of Work, but shall not include any Parts that are cancelable or otherwise transferable to IBM.

input.quote: d) The forecasts provided by IBM, or agreed to by IBM hereunder, do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product.
input.rationale: There is no take-or-pay or minimum volume obligation on us. Forecasts expressly "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product" (p0882); Products are "produced and delivered according to actual intake of IBM Customer Orders" and the forecast is only MSL's Parts-ordering authorisation (p0870); we may "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time" (p0722); and "IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility" under the Supply Flexibility appendix (p0927). The only volume-linked exposure is the Requirements Accuracy mechanic (p0903 / Appendix 2): we bear no liability for MSL's inventory while forecast accuracy stays at or above the Appendix 2 level, and below it we compensate MSL by applying stated percentages to the actual material cost of the affected machine type. That is a cost true-up for materials MSL actually procured on our forecast, not a shortfall penalty or a multi-year commitment, and we retain an unconditional exit via PO cancellation — so the bargain sits at or above the fallback and we would not redline it. Worth noting in the rationale only (not as a deviation): the Appendix 2 percentages and thresholds are redacted, so we should confirm on the business side that the incremental percentage is genuinely cost-recovery and not punitive, and that MSL's inventory exposure remains limited to Parts within published lead times (p0870) and the Supply Flexibility window.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.",
  "Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.",
  "Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.",
  "Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty."
]

input.quote: d) The forecasts provided by IBM, or agreed to by IBM hereunder, do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product.
input.rationale: There is no take-or-pay or minimum volume obligation on us. Forecasts expressly "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product" (p0882); Products are "produced and delivered according to actual intake of IBM Customer Orders" and the forecast is only MSL's Parts-ordering authorisation (p0870); we may "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time" (p0722); and "IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility" under the Supply Flexibility appendix (p0927). The only volume-linked exposure is the Requirements Accuracy mechanic (p0903 / Appendix 2): we bear no liability for MSL's inventory while forecast accuracy stays at or above the Appendix 2 level, and below it we compensate MSL by applying stated percentages to the actual material cost of the affected machine type. That is a cost true-up for materials MSL actually procured on our forecast, not a shortfall penalty or a multi-year commitment, and we retain an unconditional exit via PO cancellation — so the bargain sits at or above the fallback and we would not redline it. Worth noting in the rationale only (not as a deviation): the Appendix 2 percentages and thresholds are redacted, so we should confirm on the business side that the incremental percentage is genuinely cost-recovery and not punitive, and that MSL's inventory exposure remains limited to Parts within published lead times (p0870) and the Supply Flexibility window.

content.text:
**Finding: MINCOMMIT — compliant (no redline proposed).**

We reviewed every candidate location (Product Forecast §11.0–11.3, Purchase of Products §6.0, PO Cancellation §6.1, Inventory §13.0–13.4, Supply Flexibility §13.2/Appendix 4, Requirements Accuracy Appendix 2, Premium Cost §9.0, and Rights/Prices Upon Termination §5.2–5.3).

- **No minimum purchase or volume commitment:** forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product" (p0882); production follows "actual intake of IBM Customer Orders" (p0870).
- **Exit retained:** we may cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time (p0722); no liability for unused supply flexibility (p0927).
- **Only volume-linked exposure** is the Requirements Accuracy mechanic (p0903 / Appendix 2), which is a percentage-of-material-cost true-up for Parts MSL actually bought on our forecast — a true-up, not a shortfall penalty, and not term-length take-or-pay.
- Termination inventory buy-backs (§5.2) are bounded by Supply Flexibility and exclude cancellable Parts, so they are wind-down cost recovery rather than a purchase commitment.

The bargain therefore meets the fallback (and substantially the preferred) position, so no redline. Business-side check only: the Appendix 2 percentages/thresholds are redacted — confirm they are cost-recovery rather than punitive.

elements.evidence: Inserted Subsection 5.2 d): "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, MSL will provide the transition assistance ..." — this cures the chapeau in 5.2 a), which was limited to "expiration or termination for default".

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: New clause d) commits only to "a period of at least ninety (90) Days following such expiration or termination"; no six-month assistance period appears anywhere in the operative text.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Clause d) is silent on pricing; neither it nor Section 5.2 a) ii) contains any then-current-rates (or any charging) mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d): "within thirty (30) Days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to IBM all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for IBM that is in MSL's possession or control." (Note: "Days" is defined at 1.3 as business days.)

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Clause d) requires only that MSL "export and deliver" the data; no commonly used/machine-readable format requirement is stated, and Section 5.2 a) iii) speaks only of returning documentation and confidential media.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written-certification obligation exists in clause d) or elsewhere in the cited termination provisions.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d) opens "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason", so the assistance and export duties are not gated to default terminations.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Clause d) fixes the previously open-ended Section 5.2 a) ii) duty: "provide the transition assistance described in Subsection 5.2 a) ii) for a period of at least ninety (90) Days following such expiration or termination."

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d): export and delivery of "all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for IBM" within thirty (30) Days after expiration or termination; the scope covers every category of IBM data, not selected types.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted Subsection 5.2 d) supplies (i) an any-reason trigger, (ii) a committed minimum 90-Day assistance period anchored to the existing Section 5.2 a) ii) assistance scope, and (iii) a 30-Day export of all IBM data.

Preferred is not complete — four elements are absent from operative language: a six-month assistance period, a then-current-rates charging basis, a commonly used machine-readable return format, and post-return certified deletion. The finding correctly targets fallback only.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletion or paraphrase of existing Section 5.2 language, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural extras, and no duplication of the existing 5.2 a) iii) return of documentation/confidential media (which is a different subject matter).

Intent preserved: clause d) supplements rather than contradicts the 5.2 a) default-only chapeau and 5.2 c) inventory buy-back; the cross-reference to "Subsection 5.2 a) ii)" resolves to an existing provision, leaving no dangling reference or undefined term.

Drafting caution (not a failure): "Days" is defined at 1.3 as business days, so the 30-Day export window runs roughly six calendar weeks and the 90-Day assistance period runs roughly eighteen calendar weeks. The usage is consistent with Section 5.2 a) iii) and the defined-term convention, but if a hard calendar deadline is wanted, change the export trigger to lower-case "thirty (30) calendar days".

Optional strengthening toward preferred, if leverage allows: add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export duty and a sentence requiring MSL thereafter to delete IBM data and certify deletion in writing; add "at MSL's then-current rates" only if the parties need an express charging basis.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 5.4: "Notwithstanding Section 5.1, IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL...". IBM is Customer; the right runs to "this Agreement", which satisfies the disjunctive element (Agreement or Order Form). The narrow opener neutralises the retained "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary... for cause" preamble so the new right is operative rather than contradicted.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL" — exactly 30 days, in writing, given by Customer to Vendor. No additional conditions (no consent, no cause, no cure) are attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination." The refund obligation is on Vendor (MSL), is expressly pro rata (not merely inferred from a post-termination period), and is triggered by the convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 5.1 preamble confines termination to cause for both parties: "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows". Section 4.0's six-month "intent to terminate" notice operates against the automatic twelve-month renewal and is natural-term non-renewal, which is assessed under RENEWAL rather than as a mid-term T4C right. No new Vendor convenience right is created by the insertion, which is one-directional (IBM only).

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The drafted notice period is thirty (30) days, which is the preferred figure and sits outside the 60–90 day fallback band. This is not a defect (the preferred level is met and 30 days is more favourable to Customer); it simply means the fallback checklist is not the completed level.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the inserted Section 5.4 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty or contingent payment on Customer, so there is nothing requiring a cap. SOW Section 6.1's cost-reimbursement language addresses cancellation of individual Purchase Orders, not Agreement-level convenience termination, and is left unchanged.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 5.1 permits termination by either Party only for cause, so Vendor has no convenience right at all — a fortiori stricter than end-of-term only. Caveat for the drafter: Section 4.0's either-party six-month notice does not expressly tie its effective date to the end of the then-current term, so it cannot itself be relied on as an end-of-term restriction; it is treated here as non-renewal under RENEWAL.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor has no convenience termination right under Section 5.1. To the extent Section 4.0's non-renewal notice were characterised as a Vendor exit, it requires six (6) months' notice, which exceeds 90 days.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met by the single inserted Section 5.4 plus the retained for-cause-only Section 5.1; the fallback level is incomplete only because the notice period (30 days) is below the 60–90 day band, which is more favourable to Customer and therefore not a defect.

Deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returns false, but on inspection of the rendered operative text this is a mechanical false negative — the text expressly reads "IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL". The operative language, not the regex, controls here; the coverage and minimality gates both pass.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion for a missing clause, no deletions, no rewriting of Section 5.1, and no extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedures). The drafter correctly omitted "in whole or in part" from the model language, since no Order Form or partial-termination structure in this checklist requires it, and correctly used a narrow "Notwithstanding Section 5.1" rather than a broad override.

Intent is preserved: Sections 5.2, 5.3, Section 4.0's renewal/non-renewal mechanic and cross-reference to Section 5.0, SOW Section 6.1 Purchase Order cancellation and the Parts cost-reimbursement pricing (p0143) all survive without contradiction; the narrow notwithstanding resolves the only tension (the retained "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary... for cause" preamble).

Two drafting points to confirm rather than repair: (i) verify the retained for-cause preamble is in fact numbered Section 5.1 in the executed document, so the new cross-reference is not dangling; (ii) "fees prepaid by IBM" is descriptive rather than a defined term in this manufacturing agreement — consider "amounts prepaid by IBM" if "fees" is not used elsewhere, though this does not defeat the element.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

input.quote: Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows:
input.rationale: The Base Agreement runs for an initial three-year term (p0104) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause (breach, insolvency, competitor acquisition, force majeure). IBM therefore has no right to terminate the Agreement for convenience during a multi-year committed term, which the playbook treats as a missing-behaviour deviation. Exit today runs only through six months' non-renewal notice under Section 4.0 (a natural-term non-renewal, addressed under RENEWAL, not T4C) and IBM's purchase-order cancellation right in SOW Section 6.1, which reaches individual Purchase Orders only and carries cost reimbursement. On the other side, MSL has no mid-term convenience right: Section 5.1 confines termination by either Party to cause, so preferred element 4 is already met and we have not added a prohibition. We added the shortest preferred-level clause (new Section 5.4) giving IBM a 30-day convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; 60-90 days' notice is available as a fallback.

content.text:
**Finding submitted — T4C: missing (Customer convenience right).**

- **What the document does:** The Base Agreement has a three-year initial term (§4.0, p0104) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause — material breach, insolvency events, competitor acquisition, and continuing force majeure (§5.1, p0107–p0118). Sections 5.2/5.3 only handle post-termination inventory and pricing.
- **Other exits checked:** §4.0 six-month non-renewal notice (natural-term non-renewal → RENEWAL rule, not flagged here); SOW §2.0 twelve-month non-renewal (p0658); SOW §6.1 IBM purchase-order cancellation "at any time" (p0722) — PO-level only and subject to cost reimbursement; §16.17 force majeure termination (cause-based); AECI §8 mutual notice termination (p1497) governs only the confidentiality exchange form, not the services term.
- **Direction check:** MSL has no mid-term convenience right — §5.1's "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary … for cause" opener carries preferred element 4, so I marked it already_met rather than adding a redundant prohibition against MSL.
- **Redline (preferred, validated ok:true):** one insertion of a new §5.4 after p0143 giving IBM convenience termination on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, with the 60–90 day fallback offered in the comment. No "in whole or in part", no penalty or survival boilerplate added.
